learning: If the oval finishes stay at 18 or more of 20 and s-bend progress holds near 0.45 or above, the larger radius is adding speed without losing turn authority. If s-bend progress falls below about 0.4, the wider track is the likely cause, since 0.10 m gave 0.236 in iteration 1. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3, reduce kp in small steps before any geometry change.
notes: Builder's geometry adopted unchanged (wheel_radius 0.040 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, all sensing values from iteration 4). Controller kept at iteration 4 values so the drivetrain change is the only variable.
rationale: Iteration 4 (404.6, best) is the reference: 5 sensors at y=0.08 m, 0.015 m pitch, 0.012 m footprint, wheel_track 0.09 m, wheel_radius 0.035 m, mass 0.6 kg, with the controller base_speed 1.7, kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.4, weights -2 to +2, last_direction. Its oval finished 20 of 20 and s-bend progress was 0.486. The Builder's proposal raises wheel_radius from 0.035 to 0.040 m (about 14% more wheel speed for the same PWM) and widens wheel_track from 0.09 to 0.10 m. Sensing is unchanged, so the drivetrain is the only variable. Iteration 1 (track 0.10, y=0.07) gave s-bend progress 0.236, against 0.446 at track 0.09 (iteration 3), so a 0.10 m track alone has cost s-bend progress before. I keep the Builder's geometry as proposed to test the speed lever. For the controller I keep kp 2.5 and kd 0.4, since the ratio of radius to track is close to the iteration 4 value and the turn authority should stay similar. I keep base_speed at 1.7 so that speed comes only from the larger wheel radius and the effect stays isolated. ki 0.05 and last_direction are unchanged. Expected result: a shorter completion time than iteration 4's 1.73 s on the oval, and slalom progress above the 0.18 plateau if speed is the limit. s-bend progress is the main risk, because the wider track may cost turn authority again.
